October 8, 2026

Human Resource Department
Adolescent Wellness Academy  
Davie, Florida

Re: Adolescent Services Manager Position

Dear Hiring Personnel,

With more than a decade of experience in education, youth development, and program leadership, I am pleased to apply for the Adolescent Services Manager position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. My background reflects a strong commitment to creating safe, structured, and supportive environments where young people can thrive, while ensuring staff, daily operations, and organizational processes work together effectively.

Throughout my career, including my role as Assistant Director at Center of Life Academy and my educational leadership responsibilities with the Urban League of Greater Miami, I have gained extensive experience supervising employees, coordinating daily operations, supporting student development, and building meaningful relationships with families. These roles have strengthened my ability to set clear expectations, coach and develop staff, resolve challenges, maintain accountability, and foster a positive, collaborative environment.

My experience also includes developing and implementing social-emotional learning initiatives, coordinating youth programs, monitoring progress, maintaining documentation, and collaborating with families and community stakeholders. Additionally, two years of full-time AmeriCorps service helped establish a strong foundation in student engagement, individualized support, and community service. Together, these experiences have reinforced the importance of consistency, compassion, effective communication, and understanding young people's unique needs.

What particularly interests me about Adolescent Wellness Academy is its commitment to supporting adolescents and families through structured, compassionate care. The opportunity to contribute my operational leadership experience while collaborating with clinical professionals aligns with my passion for helping young people navigate challenges and develop the skills necessary for personal growth. My leadership approach emphasizes accountability, organization, teamwork, and maintaining an environment where staff and the individuals they serve feel supported and respected.

Thank you for considering my application. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my professional experience, leadership abilities, and dedication to youth development can contribute to the continued success of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I stumbled upon your company website and believe it is an incredible provision for so many young ones.  I currently work part time as a substitute teacher who teaches and guides students in various subjects. One subject that comes up constantly (not on the curriculum) is why people are so different. 
  I help students not only in academic areas but emotional and psychological areas that sometimes makes them feel alone or like outcasts.
When I reviewed the work that goes on at AWA, I immediately wanted to apply and find a position.  AWA is exactly what Florida and the whole world needs.  
  I enjoy helping people at all times, but helping the youth and future of our world is my passion.
While this is not the typical cover letter, what I would like to add is that I am a professional who has worked in healthcare and the school system. My goal is to do all that I can for people with compassion, empathy and the respect they deserve.
 It would be an honor to be part of a company such as AWA which does just that.

Thank you for your time,
Marilyn Vega

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to express my interest in the Clinic Director position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counselor with an Ed.D. in Community Care and Counseling: Traumatology and more than 15 years of experience in behavioral health, clinical services, and program leadership, I bring a strong commitment to providing high-quality, trauma-informed care to adolescents and families.

Throughout my career, I have worked extensively with youth experiencing complex behavioral health challenges, trauma histories, family instability, and barriers to accessing appropriate treatment. In my leadership role with Partners Health Management, I have overseen behavioral health initiatives across a 15-county service area, supervised multidisciplinary teams, and helped develop and implement specialized programs designed to improve access to services, strengthen care coordination, and reduce unnecessary higher levels of care.  One of my greatest professional strengths is combining clinical expertise with operational leadership. I have experience supporting clinical decision-making, establishing effective workflows, monitoring quality and compliance, mentoring staff, and collaborating with families, community providers, hospitals, and child welfare agencies. I understand the importance of developing a clinical environment where staff feel supported, families feel heard, and adolescents receive individualized, evidence-based treatment.

My doctoral research focused on the experiences of social workers placing youth in residential treatment within North Carolina's child welfare system. This work further strengthened my understanding of the challenges adolescents and families face when appropriate community-based behavioral health services are unavailable. I am particularly passionate about developing programs that intervene earlier, promote stability, and help youth receive effective treatment in the least restrictive appropriate setting.

The opportunity to contribute to the development and leadership of Adolescent Wellness Academy's North Carolina program is especially appealing. I would welcome the opportunity to help establish a strong clinical culture, support staff development, build community partnerships, and ensure that adolescents and families receive compassionate, effective, and accountable care.  Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, leadership background, and commitment to adolescent mental health could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's success.

Sincerely,
April L. Rorabaugh, Ed.D., LCMHC

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager, 

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Intake Coordinator position at the Adolescent Wellness Academy. I bring more than 20 years of administrative and client-support experience, bilingual English/Spanish communication skills, and a compassionate skills, and a compassionate approach to helping people navigate unfamiliar processes. I would welcome the opportunity to help adolescents and their families be heard, informed, and supported as they take the first steps toward care or continued care.

At New Jersey City University, I provided administrative support for two graduate programs, assisting with admissions, registration, scheduling and confidential academic records. This work required clear communication, accurate documentation, and coordination among students, faculty, and department leadership. As an office manager for Rental Shop LLC, I managed appointments, client communications, confidential tenant records and competing administrative priorities. These experiences prepared me to gather and organize information carefully, explain next steps clearly, and keep processes moving. 

My work as a translator and liaison with Hope Outreach Ministries for Everyone strengthened my ability to communicate across languages and cultures. In my independent wellness practice. I am comfortable using Zoom, Google Workspace, and Microsoft Office to support remote collaboration and organize daily operations.

My professional development in somatic trauma therapy, and traumatic grief has also deepened my appreciation for patient, respectful communication. I recognize that reaching out for mental health support can be a vulnerable moment for both adolescents and their caregivers. I would approach those conversations with care, maintain confidentiality, and follow your organization's intake procedures and escalation protocols closely. 

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my administrative experience, bilingual skills, and dependable follow-through to you team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to discussing how I can support your intake operations and the families you serve.

Sincerely,

Janette Yancey
862-218-9442
janetteyancey.rsd@gmail.com

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Bilingual Virtual Intake Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy.  I am passionate about mental health and particularly enjoy working with adolescents. I believe that every young person has a unique way of understanding the world, and one of the things I value most about working with them is that I learn so much from each individual and their thought process. I find it meaningful to understand their perspectives, recognize their needs, and contribute to an environment where they feel heard, respected, and supported; it matter to me the most to provide a safe space for each and everyone of them.

Through my psychology practicums, I have gained experience conducting psychological assessments with adolescents, administering and interpreting psychological tests, and participating in interventions focused on adolescent development, family unity, and violence prevention. I have also worked with children who have experienced abandonment or violence, which has strengthened my empathy and taught me the importance of approaching sensitive situations with patience, care, and professionalism.

I consider myself a highly empathetic, adaptable, and resourceful person. I learn quickly, think critically, and enjoy finding practical solutions when challenges arise. I understand that supporting adolescents and their families involves not only compassion but also organization, clear communication, and attention to detail. I am comfortable working with Zoom and digital tools, and I would be confident managing virtual interactions while helping families navigate the intake process and ensuring that information is communicated accurately to the appropriate team members.

As a native Spanish speaker with C1-level English proficiency, I can communicate effectively with families in both languages and help create a more accessible and welcoming experience. I would be excited to contribute my psychological background, interpersonal skills, and genuine interest in adolescent well-being to AWA's mission of supporting young people and their families.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, motivation, and skills could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Mariana Ochoa Ortiz

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. With more than three years of experience in healthcare, care coordination, and social services, along with my ongoing Master of Social Work studies and clinical internship at Boca Recovery Center, I bring a strong foundation in patient advocacy, behavioral health support, resource navigation, and multidisciplinary collaboration.

Throughout my career, I have supported individuals and families navigating complex healthcare needs, behavioral health challenges, and difficult life transitions. My experience includes conducting assessments, developing individualized care plans, coordinating services, documenting clinical information, and helping individuals connect with resources that support their well-being. At Boca Recovery Center, I have gained additional clinical experience working with individuals affected by substance use disorders, participating in therapeutic groups, supporting recovery-oriented goals, and developing my skills in motivational interviewing and therapeutic communication.

What draws me to AWA is your commitment to looking beyond adolescents’ behaviors to understand the emotions, experiences, and challenges behind them. I believe every young person deserves to feel heard, respected, and supported without judgment. I am passionate about helping adolescents and families navigate difficult circumstances while building trust, strengthening coping skills, and recognizing their potential for growth and recovery.

As a trilingual professional fluent in English, Portuguese, and Spanish, I also value the opportunity to support diverse populations and help families feel understood throughout their care journey. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience, compassion, adaptability, and commitment to AWA’s mission while continuing to grow professionally within a collaborative behavioral health team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background and dedication to supporting individuals and families could contribute to the work of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,  
Ruth De Azevedo

candidates.cover_letter:
Throughout my career, I have had the privilege of working with students from a variety of backgrounds and with a wide range of academic, behavioral, and emotional needs. My experience in special education has shaped not only the professional I am today, but also the way I view the importance of creating safe spaces for young people who may be navigating some of the most difficult seasons of their lives.

Much of my career has been dedicated to special education, and I currently work in a modified setting supporting high school students. I have also worked with middle and high school students in both Emotional or Behavioral Disabilities (EBD) and Intellectual Disabilities (IND) settings. These experiences have taught me that working with adolescents requires much more than structure and routine. It requires understanding that every young person has a story and recognizing that behavior can be a form of communication. Some of the most meaningful moments in my career have come from seeing a student make progress that others may have once thought was out of reach.

My commitment to young people extends beyond the classroom. I have worked with students throughout different parts of Miami, from South Miami to Overtown, and when I lived closer to the area, I also volunteered at the Overtown Youth Center. Those experiences helped reinforce how much a young person's environment and access to caring adults can influence their path. That belief is a major reason this opportunity resonates with me.

While my professional background is rooted in education, I have also developed valuable operational and organizational skills through my previous experience with Wix and Publix. At Publix, I gained hands-on experience helping manage front-of-house operations, coordinating with leadership, and working collaboratively on staff scheduling and coverage. I learned the importance of anticipating needs, communicating clearly, adjusting to unexpected changes, and ensuring that the people and resources around me were in the right place for the day to run successfully. Combined with my experience in education, behavioral support, documentation, and student safety, these skills have prepared me to contribute to a role that requires both compassion and strong operational judgment.

As I consider this next chapter in my career, I am looking for a path that allows me to continue making a meaningful difference while also being intentional about my future and my responsibilities to my family. My decision to explore a career transition is not a reflection of losing my passion for education or for working with young people. Rather, it comes from a desire to build on what I have learned, grow into new leadership opportunities, and continue serving adolescents and families in a different capacity. I hope to bring the perspective of an educator who understands that the people behind the daily operations matter just as much as the systems that keep a program running..

It would be an honor to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's mission and to help create an environment where adolescents feel supported and staff feel equipped to do their best work. Thank you for considering my application and for the work your organization does for young people and families throughout South Florida. I would welcome the opportunity to share more about my experience and how I hope to contribute to your team.

Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Boca Raton, Florida


Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

I am excited to apply for this position at this facility in this amazing area. With direct experience
as a Telemetry Technician at Aurora Medical Center and formal CNA training through Gateway
Technical College, I bring hands-on cardiac monitoring expertise, strong clinical judgment, and a
deep commitment to patient-centered care.
In my role as a Telemetry Technician, I provided continuous cardiac surveillance for patients in
acute care settings, accurately interpreting and documenting heart rhythms and identifying
arrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation, tachycardia, bradycardia, and other critical rhythm
changes. I promptly escalated abnormal findings to Registered Nurses to support rapid clinical
intervention. I also performed 12-lead EKG acquisition, ensured proper lead placement,
troubleshot monitoring interruptions, and maintained telemetry equipment to ensure continuous
and accurate cardiac observation. My role required vigilance, precision, and the ability to act
decisively in high-acuity situations — qualities essential to a Cardiovascular Tech.
Additionally, my background as a Home Health Aide has strengthened my ability to monitor
subtle patient changes, provide compassionate one-on-one care, and maintain detailed
documentation. My previous experience at Wells Fargo further developed my attention to detail,
regulatory compliance, risk awareness, and ability to exercise sound judgment within
established policies — all skills that directly translate to maintaining monitoring accuracy and
patient safety in cardiovascular care environments.
Currently enrolled in nursing school and holding active BLS and CPR certifications, I am
committed to continuous learning and clinical excellence. I am especially drawn to Mayo Clinic’s
reputation for teamwork, innovation, and uncompromising standards in cardiovascular care. I
am eager to contribute my telemetry experience, strong observational skills, and dedication to
patient safety to your cardiovascular team.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I can’t wait to join the team and have the opportunity
to further discuss how my background and clinical strengths can support the hospital’s mission
of providing outstanding patient care.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Intake Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology and a diverse professional background in behavioral health, mental health services, juvenile justice, and security leadership, I am confident in my ability to contribute to your team and support adolescents and families seeking behavioral health services.

Throughout my career, I have developed valuable experience working with individuals with behavioral and mental health needs, communicating with diverse populations, and maintaining professionalism in sensitive situations. As a Registered Behavior Technician at Babcock Center, I gained hands-on experience supporting individuals with behavioral needs and implementing individualized support strategies. My experience as a Mental Health Technician at Three Rivers Behavioral Health further strengthened my understanding of mental health care, patient support, and the importance of creating a safe and compassionate environment for individuals receiving treatment.

Additionally, my role as an Intake Sergeant with the Department of Juvenile Justice provided me with experience managing intake-related responsibilities, communicating with youth and families, maintaining accurate documentation, and navigating situations that require sound judgment, confidentiality, and attention to detail. My experience as a Site Security Supervisor with Allied Universal also strengthened my leadership, organizational, problem-solving, and communication skills.

I believe my combination of clinical support experience, intake-related responsibilities, and educational background in psychology makes me a strong candidate for this position. I understand that the intake process is often a critical first step for families seeking mental health services for their children. I would welcome the opportunity to help make that process organized, supportive, and welcoming by communicating effectively with families, gathering necessary information, coordinating next steps, and treating every individual with dignity and compassion.

I am particularly interested in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy because I value the importance of accessible mental health services for adolescents and the positive impact that early intervention and appropriate treatment can have on their lives. I would be proud to contribute my experience, professionalism, and commitment to helping young people and their families navigate the process of obtaining care.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and passion for behavioral health can contribute to the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Aj Brown

Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am excited to apply for an opportunity with Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Master of Social Work graduate with extensive experience in behavioral health, family-centered treatment, case management, and crisis intervention, I am passionate about helping adolescents navigate challenges, develop healthy coping skills, and build a foundation for long-term emotional well-being.

Throughout my career, I have worked with children, adolescents, and families experiencing complex behavioral and mental health challenges. As a Family-Centered Treatment Specialist with Saint Francis Ministries, I developed treatment plans, provided therapeutic interventions and resources, collaborated with multidisciplinary teams, and coordinated with families, schools, courts, and community providers. This experience strengthened my ability to approach each family with empathy, flexibility, and a commitment to individualized, strengths-based care.

Previously, as a Recovery Specialist with High Plains Mental Health Center, I provided community psychiatric support, psychosocial rehabilitation, and crisis intervention services for youth with serious emotional disturbances. I also participated in wraparound facilitation and developed psychosocial group curriculum for individuals ages 4–18. My earlier work as a CBS Case Manager further developed my skills in behavioral health treatment planning, resource coordination, family support, and helping young people work toward meaningful personal goals.

I believe effective adolescent care requires more than addressing immediate symptoms. It means building trust, creating a safe and supportive environment, recognizing each young person's strengths, and equipping them with skills they can carry into adulthood. My approach is grounded in trauma-informed, evidence-based, and culturally responsive care, with an emphasis on collaboration, empowerment, and sustainable progress.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical experience, interpersonal skills, and dedication to youth and family well-being to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am eager to contribute to a team that prioritizes meaningful growth and helps adolescents and their families move toward healthier futures.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background, education, and commitment to behavioral health align with the needs of your team.

Sincerely,
Jordon Snow, MSW

With an Associate’s Degree in Health and Human Services and experience in behavioral health, home health, and direct care, I would bring compassion, clear communication, and a strong commitment to helping families access support.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my education and direct-care experience could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Sarah Anne Brandon

My healthcare experience has also given me a better understanding of the importance of confidentiality, patience, and compassion. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,
I am confident of my value, experience, and expertise directly aligning with this position.
With direct experience (13+ years) in the education field and mental health services
focused on specialization in psychology and public service. Leading with genuine
passion, work ethic, people skills, approachability, problem solving, and professionalism
are some of the strengths that translate into this position. Working in mental health
services and dozens of schools for a decade in the high risk, low socio-economic status
areas of Fresno, CA has provided experience, wisdom, technique, and punctuality that I
am forever grateful for and eager to continue paying forward.
The specific work experience I have includes interning and working as the direct
assistant for the Staff Clinical Psychologist of a California state run facility (Veterans
Home of California - Fresno). Daily duties included constant documentation,
organization of case work, assessments, veteran interaction, care plan meetings,
interventions and evaluations; upholding and monitoring the well being of close to 500
veterans. If needed, additional steps required closer monitoring of veterans and/or
students/families who were more at high risk, by taking necessary actions (contingency
plans, interventions, public assistance, community outreach, etc) to ensure safety,
enrichment, and growth for youth and elderly populations. Working in education
required duties such as: managing after-school program(s) consisting of 13+ line staff,
200+ students (varying from school site to school site), including communal and faculty
interactions on a daily basis.
Experience also includes: evaluations, incident reports, investigations, i.e., handling
student/veterans and family action items on a daily basis, often requiring composed
conflict resolution. Having those difficult conversations with parents, families, and
administrators has been irreplaceable in gaining patience, diligence, and punctuality.
Examples include: engaging with someone not permitted to be on campus showing up
or custody battles with parents showing up that are not allowed to see the students. 
This field of work can be unpredictable and bring anything on any given day. I am the
point person to uphold the safety of all my students and staff and notify administration
as a mandated reporter and I have done it with the utmost professionalism and poise in
countless situations. I have the breadth and experience of work in a live action setting
daily for over a decade now. So much so that I have gained absolute composure under
any circumstances, always putting the clients’/pupils’ needs first. Additionally, the
execution of these services required meticulous documentation and data utilizing
databases/programs such as Microsoft Office, ERC, Sharepoint, Paycom, Google Drive
and more. Producing mandatory state/federal documents, creating weekly
newsletters/pamphlets to promote expanded learning programs while also keeping our
community and stakeholders attune with updates and the programs as a whole.
Caveat: Through my breadth of experience working directly in mental health/medical
settings, as well as 13 years experience doing administrative/managerial work in the
education field (i.e., expanded learning programs/after-school programs), I gained
expertise, composure, and rapport that has directly translated to the quality work ethic,
character, and dependability I possess today. Working with our community produced
daily interactions sometimes involving conflict resolution and this required an
approachable yet efficient and communicative work ethic. Straight out of high school,
navigating getting my degree, coupled with working two jobs; as the auxiliary assistant
to a clinical psychologist and facilitating state/federal funded educational programs; I
gained invaluable experience, character, poise, and punctuality that would be ideal for
this position.

candidates.cover_letter:
Cover Letter
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining your organization. With five years of experience in virtual case management as a telephonic case manager serving pregnant women and women with infants, along with my background in education and foster care, I bring a strong foundation in client advocacy, care coordination, resource navigation, education, and family support. I am passionate about helping individuals and families overcome challenges, access essential resources, and build healthier, more stable futures.

Throughout my five years in virtual case management, I have developed valuable experience supporting pregnant women and mothers with infants through telephonic outreach, education, care coordination, and connection to appropriate community resources. This experience has strengthened my ability to build rapport with clients remotely, assess individual needs, provide compassionate support, and help families navigate important services during critical stages of their lives. I understand the importance of meeting clients where they are, maintaining professional communication, and providing individualized support that promotes positive outcomes for both mothers and their children.

In addition to my professional experience, I am currently enrolled in a master’s program in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, where I am developing my knowledge and skills in mental health counseling, with a particular interest in specializing in substance use counseling. My graduate studies reflect my commitment to expanding my ability to support individuals experiencing mental health challenges, substance use concerns, and other barriers that may affect their overall well-being. I am eager to combine my practical experience with my academic training to contribute to programs that emphasize behavioral health, prevention, intervention, and holistic client care.

My background also includes experience educating and working with youth ranging from Voluntary Prekindergarten (VPK) through middle school. These opportunities have strengthened my communication, classroom management, relationship-building, and age-appropriate teaching skills. Additionally, I have experience working in a foster home setting with children from birth through age 17, where I supported children across a wide range of developmental stages and needs. My responsibilities included leading groups and creating supportive environments that encouraged engagement, positive interactions, personal development, and emotional growth.

These combined experiences have provided me with a well-rounded understanding of the challenges faced by children, families, and vulnerable populations. I bring compassion, adaptability, strong interpersonal skills, and a commitment to treating every individual with dignity and respect. I am confident that my experience in case management, youth education, foster care, and ongoing graduate studies would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your team.

This position has strengthened my ability to recognize individual needs, respond to behavioral challenges, and provide trauma-informed support while maintaining appropriate boundaries and promoting safety.
Previously, I worked at Compass Health as an ACT Counselor, providing intensive community-based behavioral health services to adults experiencing significant mental health challenges. My experience included treatment planning, crisis intervention, coping skills development, medication education, resource coordination, and collaboration with interdisciplinary teams. This experience gave me a strong understanding of the importance of individualized care, consistency, and meeting people where they are in their recovery.
I hold a Master’s degree in Psychology from Northcentral University and have experience working with individuals facing a wide range of emotional, behavioral, and mental health challenges. My background has taught me that meaningful progress often begins when a person feels safe, respected, understood, and supported. I believe in approaching each individual with patience, empathy, accountability, and an understanding that their challenges do not define their potential.
I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's work in supporting adolescents and promoting emotional and behavioral wellness. I am committed to continued professional growth and would bring a strong work ethic, compassion, and a genuine desire to make a positive difference in the lives of the individuals and families I serve.
Thank you for considering my application. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my education, experience, and commitment to behavioral health could benefit your team. I look forward to hearing from you.
Sincerely,
Christy Davis

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining your team at your recovery facility. As a Certified Chemical Dependency Assistant (CDCA) and a certified Peer Support Specialist, I am passionate about helping individuals overcome substance use disorders, navigate the challenges of recovery, and build healthier, more fulfilling lives.

I believe that recovery is possible for everyone, and I want to be part of a team that helps individuals recognize their potential and work toward lasting change. My certifications have strengthened my knowledge of addiction, recovery principles, ethical boundaries, and the importance of providing compassionate, person-centered support. I understand the importance of meeting people where they are in their recovery journey and treating every individual with dignity, respect, and understanding.

My personal experiences have also given me a strong appreciation for the challenges people face when working toward recovery. I understand the importance of encouragement, patience, accountability, and having someone who believes in you when you are struggling to believe in yourself. I want to use my knowledge, skills, and lived experience to help others feel supported, empowered, and hopeful about their futures.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my passion for recovery, commitment to helping others, and dedication to professional growth to your organization. I am eager to continue learning, contribute to a supportive treatment environment, and make a meaningful difference in the lives of the individuals and families you serve.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications, passion, and commitment to recovery could make me a valuable addition to your team.

I am writing to express my interest in joining Adolescence Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor’s degree in Sociology and approximately two and a half years of experience working in behavioral health and social detox services at Axis Health, I have developed a strong appreciation for the importance of compassionate, individualized care and the role that supportive environments play in a person's overall well-being. I am excited about the opportunity to apply my experience and skills toward supporting adolescents and contributing to their growth, wellness, and recovery.

During my time at Axis Health, I gained hands-on experience supporting individuals in vulnerable situations, monitoring vital signs, assisting with medication administration, maintaining accurate clinical documentation, and collaborating with other professionals to support patient care. This experience strengthened my communication, organization, and problem-solving skills while teaching me the importance of approaching each individual with patience, empathy, professionalism, and respect.

My educational background in Sociology has also shaped my interest in understanding how people's environments, relationships, and life experiences influence their well-being. I believe these perspectives are especially valuable when working with adolescents, who may be navigating significant emotional, social, and developmental challenges. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to a team that prioritizes their well-being and helps them build the skills and support systems they need to move forward.

In addition to my healthcare experience, my work in customer-facing and supervisory roles has strengthened my adaptability, dependability, and ability to communicate effectively with people from diverse backgrounds. I understand the importance of maintaining professional boundaries, protecting confidential information, working collaboratively, and remaining calm and solution-focused in challenging situations.

I am eager to continue growing professionally in the behavioral health field and would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my experience, strong work ethic, and genuine interest in helping others to Adolescence Wellness Academy. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills could contribute to your team and the adolescents you serve.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Admissions Coordinator position with your organization. With a professional background in behavioral health, crisis intervention, adolescent residential treatment, and child welfare services, I believe my experience has prepared me to support adolescents and families seeking mental health and substance use treatment.

Previously, I worked as a Crisis Counselor at LifePath Systems, where I assisted with patient admissions, facilitated psychiatric evaluations, and helped individuals understand their diagnoses and treatment plans. This experience gave me an understanding of the importance of compassionate communication, timely coordination, and providing reassurance to individuals entering treatment.

Additionally, my experience as a Lead Counselor at Rite of Passage allowed me to work directly with adolescent girls facing mental health challenges, behavioral concerns, and histories of trauma. Through this position, I developed strong interpersonal skills and learned how important patience, empathy, and consistency are when working with vulnerable youth.

More recently, my work with Empower has allowed me to continue supporting young people and families through life skills education, resource coordination, and community partnerships. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to manage multiple priorities, communicate effectively, and advocate for individuals who need additional support.

I am especially drawn to this opportunity because I understand how important the first interaction with a treatment provider can be for adolescents and their families. I would strive to ensure that every individual feels respected, supported, and informed throughout the admissions process.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background, dedication, and passion for helping young people would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Sincerely,

Tia Tackett

I am a dedicated human services professional with experience in behavioral health, crisis intervention, adolescent residential treatment, patient admissions, and child welfare services. It has enabled me to develop an exceptionally heightened level of visual focus, deep attentiveness, and strong written engagement. These specialized capabilities allow me to give my complete, uninterrupted concentration to text-based inquiries, making me exceptionally proficient at engaging with families, managing online application workflows, and responding to sensitive digital correspondence with extreme clarity, care, and deep empathy.

This role, along with my practicum experience at Margarito A. Duavit Integrated School, sharpened my skills in crisis management, digital intake processing, and standardizing student and client records while maintaining absolute information privacy. Furthermore, my certifications from the Department of Health (DOH) Academy in MHPSS and the DICT Digital Workforce Hub provide me with the modern tech literacy and psychological readiness necessary to handle the digital systems and sensitive enrollment data vital to this role.

I am eager to bring my resilience, academic background in counseling, and highly focused administrative skillset to your dedicated team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I am excited about the opportunity to discuss how my unique perspectives and skills can help the Adolescent Wellness Academy continue to make a meaningful impact on adolescent mental health.


Sincerely,
Shaina Mae R. Samiana

candidates.cover_letter:
Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. After learning about this opportunity, I felt strongly compelled to apply because it combines several areas that I am genuinely passionate about: healthcare, helping individuals and families navigate difficult circumstances, providing compassionate support, and making a meaningful difference in the lives of others. With my extensive background in healthcare, medical records, pharmacy services, childcare administration, customer service, and leadership, I believe I would bring a valuable combination of professionalism, empathy, organizational skills, and dedication to your admissions team.
Throughout my professional career, I have developed a strong foundation in working with individuals from many different backgrounds, understanding their unique needs, maintaining confidentiality, and providing exceptional service during both routine and challenging situations. I understand that families seeking mental health or substance use treatment for their adolescents may be experiencing some of the most overwhelming, emotional, and uncertain moments of their lives. I believe these families deserve to be welcomed with patience, kindness, understanding, and reassurance from the very first interaction. As a Virtual Admissions Coordinator, I would take that responsibility seriously and strive to ensure that every individual who contacts your organization feels heard, respected, supported, and valued.
My professional experience includes two years working in a physician’s office managing medical records, where I developed an understanding of healthcare documentation, patient confidentiality, HIPAA regulations, accuracy, and the importance of handling sensitive information with discretion. This experience strengthened my attention to detail, organizational abilities, and understanding of how essential accurate communication and documentation are within a healthcare environment. I recognize that admissions coordination requires careful information gathering, timely follow-up, accurate recordkeeping, and effective communication between families and treatment professionals. I am confident in my ability to apply these transferable skills to support a smooth, organized, and compassionate admissions experience.
Additionally, my background as a Pharmacy Technician provided me with valuable exposure to healthcare terminology, patient interactions, medication-related processes, and the importance of professionalism in a healthcare setting. Working in healthcare has taught me that every individual has a different story, and that patience, compassion, and clear communication can make an extraordinary difference in someone’s experience. I understand the importance of maintaining appropriate professional boundaries while still providing genuine care and reassurance.
One of the most meaningful aspects of my professional background is my extensive experience in childcare, including serving as a Childcare Director for several years. In this leadership position, I was responsible for overseeing daily operations, communicating with parents and guardians, supervising employees, addressing concerns, maintaining documentation, and creating a safe, welcoming, and supportive environment for children and their families. This experience taught me how to approach sensitive conversations with understanding, remain calm when emotions are high, and build trusting relationships with families.
Having worked closely with children and their parents, I understand how deeply families care about their children’s safety, emotional well-being, and future. I recognize that parents seeking adolescent mental health or substance use treatment may feel frightened, exhausted, confused, or unsure of where to turn. I would approach every conversation without judgment and with the understanding that reaching out for help can require tremendous courage. My goal would be to make the admissions process feel less intimidating by providing clear information, answering questions within my role, communicating next steps, and helping families feel supported throughout the process.
In my current role as a Lead Resident Assistant in an assisted living facility, I continue to strengthen my leadership, communication, problem-solving, and caregiving abilities. I am responsible for helping oversee staff, ensuring procedures are followed, assisting residents with their daily needs, and maintaining a respectful and supportive environment. This position requires patience, emotional awareness, adaptability, and the ability to remain professional under pressure. I regularly interact with individuals who may be experiencing loneliness, uncertainty, frustration, or personal challenges, and I have learned that sometimes the most meaningful thing we can offer someone is our time, attention, compassion, and willingness to listen.
I also bring strong customer service and interpersonal skills. I genuinely enjoy communicating with people, establishing positive relationships, resolving concerns, and helping others find solutions. I consider myself approachable, dependable, highly motivated, and someone who takes pride in making people feel comfortable. I understand that in a virtual admissions position, communication is especially important because families may form their first impression of an organization through a telephone call, email, or online interaction. I would work diligently to ensure that each interaction reflects the professionalism, compassion, and commitment to care that Adolescent Wellness Academy strives to provide.
I am comfortable managing multiple responsibilities, prioritizing time-sensitive tasks, maintaining organized records, and learning new technology and software systems. My previous positions have required strong attention to detail, accountability, adaptability, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively. I understand the importance of responding promptly to inquiries, following established admissions procedures, coordinating information accurately, and ensuring that important details are communicated appropriately to the treatment team.
Although my professional background has included several areas of healthcare and childcare leadership rather than a position dedicated exclusively to behavioral health admissions, I am extremely eager to expand my knowledge in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. I am a dedicated learner who welcomes training, constructive feedback, and opportunities for professional growth. I understand the importance of following clinical guidance, respecting the limits of my role, and helping connect families with qualified professionals who can address their specific treatment needs.
What particularly draws me to this opportunity is the chance to contribute to an organization dedicated to helping adolescents work toward healthier, more hopeful futures. I believe that young people deserve compassion, understanding, encouragement, and access to appropriate support, especially when facing challenges that can affect their emotional well-being, relationships, and overall quality of life. I would be honored to play even a small part in helping families take that important first step toward receiving care.
I am also very interested in the virtual aspect of this position. I am confident in my ability to remain productive, focused, organized, and accountable while working remotely. I have a dedicated, quiet space in my home that would allow me to conduct professional conversations, maintain concentration, and handle responsibilities with the discretion and attention they deserve. I understand that working remotely requires self-discipline, strong communication, reliability, and consistent follow-through, and these are qualities I would bring to my work every day.
Above all, I want to be part of a team where my work has genuine purpose. I am not simply seeking another position; I am seeking an opportunity to build a meaningful, long-term career with an organization whose mission centers on helping people during vulnerable and important moments in their lives. I would bring a strong work ethic, a compassionate heart, a willingness to go above and beyond, and a sincere commitment to representing Adolescent Wellness Academy with integrity and professionalism.

Thank you for taking the time to review my application and consider me for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. I would be truly grateful for the opportunity to discuss how my professional experience, transferable skills, and genuine passion for helping others could contribute to your admissions team. I am enthusiastic about the possibility of joining Adolescent Wellness Academy and supporting the important work your organization does for adolescents and their families.

I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you.

Sincerely,

Ansleigh Davidson

For many years I have had a great interest in the helping profession. I feel that this is exactly the opportunity that I have been looking for. I like the idea of an organization who puts the people they serve first. Everyone you come across in life you have the ability to impact their life in some way, but especially in human services/ helping professions, what you say, what you do, and how you react can impact them for the better or worse, and I want to be that better. I want to help people and be that person that provides a good experience, making those big scary situations feel even just a little more okay. Everybody you come across in your day to day is somebody's cherished family member, and should be treated the same as you would treat your own family. I have spent a significant amount of time volunteering and serving the community in various ways which sparked my interest to help and serve others from a young age. Working as an EMT for over two years now I have learned that I thrive in a fast-paced environment and I love meeting new people. Additionally I’ve learned that in an ever changing environment, you are forced to constantly adapt and grow your skill set. I value the importance in every detail and how they affect the much bigger picture. People can count on me as being reliable whether they are in need of a helping hand or just a shoulder to cry on. I strive to be seen as trusted and reliable to all the people I may meet. You can never go wrong with kindness and compassion towards others. I look forward to hearing from you soon.
If you have any questions please feel free to contact me at (209) 482-8285.

Sincerely,
Zoe Kopecki

candidates.summary:
I believe my educational background in human studies, combined with my professional experience in intake and mental health services, makes me a strong candidate for this role. My experience has allowed me to develop a well-rounded understanding of client-centered care, trauma-informed communication, and the importance of meeting individuals where they are.

As an Intake & Diversion Specialist at FrontLine Service, I supported members of Cuyahoga County’s homeless community and developed valuable skills in phone-based service, trauma-informed communication, crisis support, and electronic record documentation. This role strengthened my ability to communicate effectively with individuals experiencing difficult and often complex circumstances while maintaining empathy, professionalism, and respect.

At Carrington Youth Academy, I further developed my ability to provide trauma-informed, client-centered care in a face-to-face setting. I served as a positive role model for adolescents who were navigating behavioral and mental health challenges, helping them develop healthier ways to regulate their emotions and behaviors. This experience taught me the importance of patience, consistency, and building genuine connections with clients.

I currently work at Ethan Crossing, an addiction treatment facility, where I have the opportunity to conduct admissions for clients seeking treatment for substance use disorders. This position has further strengthened my communication, assessment, and interpersonal skills while reinforcing my passion for helping individuals take meaningful steps toward recovery.

Each position I have held has contributed to my personal and professional growth and has given me a greater sense of purpose in the work I do. I am passionate about supporting others and creating a safe, compassionate environment where clients feel heard and respected. I also make a conscious effort to practice healthy coping mechanisms and self-care in my own life, allowing me to model the same principles of wellness and self-compassion that I encourage in the clients I serve. I believe this combination of professional experience, personal growth, and genuine passion for helping others would allow me to make a meaningful contribution in this role.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With more than 10 years of experience in case management, family services, client support, and highly regulated programs, along with extensive remote-work experience, I believe my background aligns well with the compassionate and organized approach required for this role.

Throughout my career, I have worked directly with children, adolescents, adults, and families who were often navigating stressful and sensitive circumstances. In my case management roles, I conducted interviews and assessments, identified client needs and potential concerns, coordinated behavioral health, medical, educational, and community services, provided referrals, maintained consistent follow-up, and carefully documented case activity.

Most recently, as a remote Unification Specialist with The Providencia Group/8-Koi, I independently managed a caseload of more than 25 cases while communicating regularly with children, families, sponsors, service providers, and other professionals. My responsibilities required strong follow-through, attention to detail, confidentiality, and the ability to explain complicated requirements in a way that families could understand. I maintained more than 95% on-time case performance and 100% audit compliance.

I also bring Medicaid and public-benefits experience through Texas Health and Human Services Commission, as well as bilingual English and Spanish communication skills. I am comfortable speaking with clients and families by phone, gathering sensitive information, coordinating appointments and services, maintaining electronic records, and learning new CRM and EMR platforms.

What especially interests me about this opportunity is the chance to be a supportive first point of contact for individuals and families seeking help. I understand that someone calling about mental health or substance use treatment may be overwhelmed, uncertain, or experiencing one of the most difficult moments of their life. I would approach each interaction with patience, empathy, professionalism, and a focus on helping the caller understand the next step.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my case management experience, bilingual communication skills, remote-work discipline, and commitment to helping families to your admissions team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

Ruby Arrieta

Dear Hiring Committee,
I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position for your adolescent mental health and substance use treatment program. With nearly five years of direct experience conducting patient admissions, intake, and discharge planning at Odyssey House Briscoe, combined with a comprehensive background managing supportive care programs and youth counseling, I am well-equipped to guide young individuals and their families through the compassionate intake process required for successful recovery.  
During my tenure at Odyssey House Briscoe, I managed admissions and discharges for individuals entering 28-day substance abuse rehabilitation programs. My primary responsibility was navigating complex intake procedures while providing empathetic support to individuals facing critical life transitions. I worked closely with clients to connect them with Medicaid coverage and ensured continuity of care by coordinating placements into sober living homes and long-term care environments upon program completion. This hands-on experience in intake coordination and step-down planning gave me a deep understanding of the recovery pipeline and the vital importance of securing a safe, supportive post-treatment environment.  
In addition to my adult and community-based substance abuse experience, I possess valuable experience working directly with youth as a Youth Counselor at BeauCARE, where I provided guidance, structure, and supervision to children. My academic background in Criminal Justice, Criminology, and Sociology, along with my recent leadership as a Program Coordinator at Gulf Coast Social Services, has further sharpened my skills in crisis de-escalation, individualized care planning, and strict adherence to client confidentiality.  
Working remotely requires high self-motivation, meticulous organization, and reliable communication. Across my various administrative and program coordination roles, I have consistently demonstrated the ability to handle high-pressure environments with professionalism, adaptability, and discretion. I am adept at navigating digital records and case management systems, making virtual admissions and multi-disciplinary team collaboration a seamless process.  
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in intake coordination, passion for youth and adolescent care, and dedicated work ethic align with the needs of your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration.  
Sincerely,
Joseph Potts

Ciearra Lockley
Bronx, NY

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With experience supporting youth and families in behavioral health programming, coordinating communication, maintaining accurate records, and connecting participants with appropriate resources, I am eager to contribute to your mission of helping adolescents access the support and treatment they need.

In my previous role as a Youth Advocate and Data Coordinator with Vibrant Emotional Health, I supported youth ages 15–23 and their families through participant engagement, follow-up communication, resource coordination, and program documentation. I maintained accurate participant records in the AWARDS electronic health record system, tracked engagement and program progress, coordinated meetings, and collaborated with program staff and community partners to support continuity of services. This experience strengthened my ability to communicate professionally, manage sensitive information, stay organized, and approach each interaction with empathy and respect.

I understand that seeking behavioral health or substance use treatment can be a difficult and vulnerable experience for adolescents and their families. I would bring a compassionate, nonjudgmental, and organized approach to helping families navigate the admissions process, understand program requirements, complete necessary steps, and connect with the appropriate team members. I am comfortable managing multiple responsibilities, communicating across teams, and maintaining careful attention to documentation and confidentiality.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my background in youth engagement, behavioral health program support, and administrative coordination to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and commitment to supporting young people align with your team’s needs.

Sincerely,
Ciearra Lockley

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over 13 years of experience in healthcare, including direct patient care, administrative management, human resources, and operational leadership, I believe I have developed a valuable combination of compassion, communication skills, organization, and professionalism that would translate well into this position.

Throughout my healthcare career, I have had the opportunity to work with individuals and families during some of the most difficult and vulnerable moments of their lives. My experience in hospice care, hospitals, and residential services has taught me the importance of patience, empathy, active listening, and providing reassurance when someone may be feeling overwhelmed or uncertain. I understand that the first person someone speaks with when seeking help can make a lasting impression, and I take that responsibility seriously. I strive to ensure that every individual feels heard, respected, and supported.

As I progressed into administrative and leadership positions, I developed strong skills in managing multiple responsibilities, maintaining accurate and confidential records, coordinating services, communicating with healthcare professionals, and ensuring timely follow-through on important matters. In my current position as Director of Operations Designee, I am accustomed to independently managing priorities, resolving unexpected challenges, maintaining regulatory compliance, and ensuring that important tasks and communications do not fall through the cracks. I am comfortable navigating computer-based systems, learning new technology, and maintaining the attention to detail necessary when handling sensitive information.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to combine my healthcare background with my administrative strengths while continuing to make a meaningful difference in people's lives. I recognize that behavioral health admissions involves specialized knowledge, and I am genuinely eager to expand my understanding of PHP and IOP services, insurance verification, admissions procedures, and the systems utilized by your organization. I have always enjoyed learning new skills and challenging myself professionally, and my career progression reflects my ability to adapt quickly, take initiative, and grow into new responsibilities.

While my background has primarily been in direct care, healthcare administration, and developmental disabilities services rather than dedicated behavioral health admissions, I am confident in the transferable skills I bring to this opportunity. I am highly motivated, dependable, compassionate, and willing to put in the effort necessary to become knowledgeable and successful in this role. I would welcome the opportunity to prove myself, learn from your team, and demonstrate the value I could bring to your admissions process.

I am particularly drawn to the mission of helping individuals and families take that first step toward receiving the support they need. Whether assisting an adolescent and their family or an adult seeking treatment and recovery, I would approach every interaction with the same compassion, respect, professionalism, and commitment to follow-through that have guided me throughout my healthcare career.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would greatly appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience, dedication, and willingness to learn could contribute to your team. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely,

Danica Heath

To Whom It May Concern,


I am writing to apply for a full-time position you may have available and will happily consider a full variety of roles that would meet your needs at your convenience. I have a variety of skills, knowledge, abilities and believe in giving relentless effort in care for both my job responsibilities and for people I may serve AND work alongside. I am confident I can adjust to many service, support or labor roles. I believe my personality and work traits fit into several work environments if I am given the chance. 

I have worked in student services/college administration, behavioral healthcare and athletic coaching for many years. I am accustomed to maintaining high standards of organization, management of/collaboration with individuals and teams, problem-solving various circumstances, giving relentless effort, meeting deadlines, writing and documenting accurately and thoroughly, utilizing various software platforms, navigating policies and procedures, and reliably serving customer/client needs. My resume may appear long and winding – but I am in strong need of change of both scenery and responsibility. I have grown emotionally fatigued by clinical mental healthcare and ultimately have left the profession due to the multiple effects of burnout. I can no longer serve the high standards that the job requires; as such, I will be giving up my licenses to practice. 

To maintain my own health and wellness, I believe transition is necessary. At this stage, I am providing private hitting lessons as a long time baseball and softball coach while recovering from a spring-time eye surgery. I am now healthy and ready to move forward. I wish to pursue employment in a more dynamic, open-air environment where I can still serve people and processes and my teammates. In essence, I want to show up to a world-class organization, work extremely hard, make people’s lives easier and return home to my family and sports endeavors. I wish to do this without bringing my work home with me, in a way; I long to return to a more transactional service environment as part of a great team while minimizing the burden of working in long-term healthcare. I can no longer operate defining myself by a career that has become impossible to engage in meaningfully; rather, I wish to operate being defined by HOW I engage in my job.

I would love to talk with you further about this – I only write this letter to briefly clarify my intent and explain my situation, as I know my resume background may seem incongruent and/or leave you with questions. 



Best Regards,

	

Greg Jurica

Sincerely,
Paul Wyche
