Stephanie Mikkelson Smith
Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator, Substance Use Treatment


I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Principles Recovery Center. With over eight years of experience in recovery services and hands-on experience coordinating substance use disorder treatment admissions from initial contact through placement and beyond, I bring a strong combination of compassion, persistence, communication skills, and professional knowledge to this position.

Throughout my career, I have worked directly with individuals experiencing substance use disorders, co-occurring mental health conditions, and significant barriers to accessing treatment. My professional experience includes serving as a Recovery Coach with Forest County Wellness Court and an IPS Employment Specialist with North Central Health Care.

One of my greatest strengths is my ability to guide individuals through the entire treatment admissions process. I have personally helped people identify appropriate treatment facilities, communicated directly with admissions departments, coordinated placements, addressed barriers, and followed through to ensure successful admission. My involvement does not end when someone enters treatment. I recognize the importance of continued communication, follow-up, and support throughout the recovery process.

I understand that successful admissions coordination requires more than answering inquiries. It involves building trust, addressing concerns, maintaining consistent follow-up, and helping prospective clients move from considering treatment to actively entering it. I am confident in my ability to establish rapport quickly, communicate effectively over the telephone, and help individuals and families make informed decisions during challenging circumstances.

My approach is grounded in motivational interviewing, trauma-informed care, person-centered services, and respect for multiple pathways to recovery. I have completed Wisconsin peer support training and have additional training in recovery coaching, sexual assault advocacy, and trauma-informed care.

I am also pursuing associate degrees in Human Services and Substance Use Disorder Counseling at Northcentral Technical College, where I have maintained a 4.0 GPA.

What particularly attracts me to Principles Recovery Center is the opportunity to combine my passion for helping individuals achieve recovery with my strengths in admissions coordination, client engagement, and treatment placement.

I understand that every inquiry represents someone who may be taking one of the most important steps of their life. I take that responsibility seriously. I do not simply help individuals find treatment. I work to ensure they successfully access it, and I remain invested in their continued progress.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and commitment to recovery to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how my qualifications and experience can contribute to the continued success of Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

Stephanie Mikkelson Smith

candidates.cover_letter:
Hello and good afternoon!
I've spent 15 years working with people in recovery, and I've seen how much that first conversation matters. If the person on the other end is calm, clear, and actually listening, people show up. If not, a lot of them don't. That's why the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role caught my attention.
Right now I'm a Wellness Specialist at New Hope Ranch, a residential rehab in Manor, Texas, run by Discovery Behavioral Health. My days are spent with clients who are early in recovery, often scared, sometimes guarded, and almost always dealing with more than one thing at once. I work alongside our clinical team, and I know how a client moves from intake through detox, residential, and into step-down care like PHP and IOP. When a family asks what the next level of care looks like, I can explain it in plain language because I see it every day.
Before this work, I spent years teaching personal training, meditation, and yoga. I also run my own coaching business, Phone Habits, where I help people build healthier relationships with their phones. Running that business taught me the practical side of this job: following up with people who are on the fence, keeping track of who I talked to and what they need, and not letting anyone fall through the cracks. I'm comfortable working on my own, staying organized, and getting things done without someone looking over my shoulder.
I'm also invested in growing in this field. I have an associate degree in psychology, I'll finish my bachelor's in the next couple of months, and I'm studying for my Texas LCDC certification. I understand confidentiality and HIPAA from working in treatment, and I pick up new systems quickly. I also have plenty of experience with KIPU, if it helps. What I'd bring to your admissions team is simple. I know how to talk to people on one of the worst days of their life, and I know how to get them to the next step. I'd love the chance to talk with you about how I can help more people make it through your door.
Thank you so much for your time! Talk soon. Ryan.

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. My background combines medical office administration, behavioral health experience, special education, and client-facing service. I believe these experiences have prepared me to help individuals and families navigate the admissions process with compassion, organization, and professionalism.

During my time at Clean Slate Centers, I supported daily medical office operations, including patient scheduling, insurance eligibility verification, prior authorizations, patient and pharmacy follow-up, medical record maintenance, and retention tracking. I worked with confidential patient information and followed HIPAA and CARF requirements. This experience taught me the importance of accurate documentation, timely communication, and dependable follow-through in a behavioral healthcare setting.

My work in special education has further strengthened my communication and coordination skills. As a one-to-one paraprofessional and job/skills coach, I have supported individuals with diverse needs, collaborated with families and professional staff, helped establish individualized goals, coordinated schedules, and monitored progress. These responsibilities require patience, adaptability, sound judgment, and the ability to communicate respectfully with people in different circumstances.

In addition, my previous leadership and training experience in customer service has prepared me to manage competing priorities, build rapport, resolve concerns, and maintain a professional approach in a fast-paced environment.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my healthcare administration experience, attention to detail, and people-centered approach to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I understand that the admissions process can be an important first step for families seeking support, and I would strive to make that interaction organized, informative, and welcoming.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Anastasia Zmarzly

Dear Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in the Remote Admissions Counselor position at Wellness Academy. With a background in human services, residential counseling, behavioral support, and case management, combined with my personal experience in addiction recovery, I believe I would bring a unique and valuable perspective to your admissions team.

My connection to the recovery community is both professional and personal. I have nearly four years of sobriety, have spent four years living in sober living environments, and have experience serving as a sober living house manager. I regularly attend recovery meetings and serve as a sponsor to others. These experiences have given me firsthand insight into the challenges individuals face when seeking treatment, building a support network, and maintaining long-term recovery. I understand the importance of meeting people where they are, treating them with dignity, and helping them feel comfortable taking the first step toward getting help.

Professionally, I have worked for nearly two years as a residential counselor supporting at-risk youth and have experience with crisis prevention and de-escalation. I have also spent over four years working with vulnerable populations, including individuals with disabilities, in direct support and other human services roles. My additional experience includes working with the YMCA in underserved urban communities facing financial hardship and gang-related challenges, as well as providing support involving case management and individualized care planning. I am trained in Registered Behavior Technician principles and am CPR certified. These roles have strengthened my ability to communicate with people from diverse backgrounds, navigate challenging situations, and provide compassionate, person-centered support.

I am currently completing my Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, which I expect to finish in December 2026, and plan to begin my Master of Social Work program in January 2027. My long-term goal is to build a career helping individuals and families access the resources and services they need to improve their lives. I see admissions counseling as an important part of that mission because connecting someone with appropriate treatment can be the beginning of meaningful change.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my lived experience, human services background, and commitment to recovery to Wellness Academy. I am especially interested in helping individuals and families navigate the admissions process with compassion, professionalism, and encouragement during what can be a vulnerable and overwhelming time. I would be proud to contribute to a team dedicated to helping people take the next step toward recovery and wellness.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, education, and passion for helping others could contribute to Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Caroline Fortney

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Substance Use Treatment position with Principles Recovery Center. With extensive experience in behavioral health, substance use recovery support, case management, medical administration, and healthcare coordination, I believe my background aligns well with your mission of helping individuals access the treatment and support they need to begin their recovery journey.

In my current role as a Recovery Specialist with Northeastern Center, I provide recovery-focused support and guidance to individuals experiencing behavioral health and substance use challenges. I collaborate with interdisciplinary teams, assist with individualized treatment planning, maintain detailed documentation, and help connect clients with appropriate services and resources. This experience has strengthened my ability to communicate compassionately with individuals who may be experiencing difficult circumstances while maintaining professionalism, confidentiality, and a client-centered approach.

Previously, as a Case Manager with Northeastern Center, I developed individualized service plans, supported clients in achieving treatment goals, coordinated with community agencies and other professionals, and provided crisis intervention and daily living skills support. My experience as a Mental Health Technician in an inpatient psychiatric setting also provided valuable exposure to patient admissions, intake procedures, monitoring, and therapeutic support. Additionally, my experience as a Care Home Supervisor strengthened my organizational, leadership, staff coordination, and communication skills.

Throughout my healthcare career, I have developed strong documentation, recordkeeping, and follow-through skills, along with experience working with multidisciplinary teams to coordinate services and support positive outcomes. My background in medical assisting has further strengthened my understanding of healthcare operations, patient communication, and the importance of accurate records and confidentiality. I am comfortable managing multiple responsibilities, communicating by phone, and maintaining organized records while ensuring that individuals feel respected and supported throughout the process.

I also hold a Certified Peer Support Professional credential and have completed additional education and training in psychology, mental health, substance abuse treatment, cognitive behavioral therapy, and motivational interviewing. These qualifications complement my professional experience and reinforce my commitment to helping individuals navigate treatment options, overcome barriers to care, and take meaningful steps toward recovery.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my behavioral health experience, recovery-focused perspective, communication skills, and dedication to client care to Principles Recovery Center. I understand that the admissions process is often a critical first step for individuals and families seeking help, and I would be committed to providing compassionate, timely communication while supporting efficient coordination between prospective clients, admissions staff, and clinical teams.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications could contribute to the continued success of Principles Recovery Center and the individuals you serve.

Sincerely,
Desiree Rowe

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Principles Recovery Center Hiring Team,

I think one of the most important things we can do for someone seeking treatment is make sure they don't regret reaching out. That might sound simple, but I know how much vulnerability can come with asking for help, especially when substance use, mental health, family relationships, and financial concerns are all tangled together. Someone might be ready to make a change and still be terrified of what comes next. I want to be the person who makes that next step feel a little less overwhelming, who takes the time to listen, answers questions without judgment, and follows through on what I say I'm going to do.

That's why the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Principles Recovery Center caught my attention. I care deeply about making treatment accessible, but I also recognize how much work happens between someone deciding they want help and actually receiving it.

At Traverse Therapy, I work with clients and families, many of whom are adolescents navigating their own mental health challenges. I've seen how important thoughtful communication, patience, and consistency are, especially when someone is already overwhelmed by the process of accessing care. My crisis counselor experience with VCC has further shaped how I approach people in vulnerable situations. I've learned to be comfortable with difficult conversations, to listen for what someone is really communicating, and to respect their autonomy even when their path forward looks different from what someone else might choose for them.

I also bring nearly a decade of healthcare experience, including pharmacy operations, insurance authorizations, confidential records, and care coordination. I know firsthand how frustrating healthcare systems can be to navigate, and I genuinely enjoy working through the details that help people get where they need to be. I'm comfortable with electronic health records, including SimplePractice, and with managing responsibilities independently. I understand that in admissions, a missed follow-up or an unanswered question can mean losing an opportunity to connect someone with care.

I'm currently pursuing degrees in substance use disorder counseling and social work. My studies have strengthened my commitment to person-centered, trauma-informed, and harm-reduction approaches. I believe people deserve to have a meaningful say in their treatment, and that building trust starts with understanding their circumstances rather than making assumptions about them.

I was especially interested in Principles Recovery Center's individualized approach to treatment, including your PHP and IOP programs and support for people experiencing co-occurring mental health conditions. I appreciate the importance of helping someone understand which services may fit their needs while coordinating with clinical staff to ensure they receive appropriate care. I also understand the operational side of admissions, from keeping referrals organized and following up consistently to maintaining accurate documentation and helping the process move forward.

I would be excited to contribute to a team where I can bring together my healthcare experience, crisis support background, and genuine passion for substance use treatment. I care about doing this work well because the people reaching out deserve both kindness and someone they can count on.

Thank you for considering my application. I would love the opportunity to speak with you.

Warmly,
Amanda Kissinger

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Principles Recovery Center. With my background in case management, behavioral health, administrative coordination, and supporting individuals experiencing substance use disorders and mental health challenges, I believe I would bring a unique combination of professional experience, compassion, and dedication to your admissions team. Helping individuals access the resources they need to begin their recovery journey is something I am genuinely passionate about.

Throughout my professional experience, I have worked with individuals facing serious and persistent mental illness, substance use disorders, and significant barriers to accessing healthcare and community resources. My background in case management and healthcare linkage has given me valuable experience coordinating services, supporting clients through difficult situations, maintaining confidential documentation, and helping individuals navigate complex systems. I have also worked with incarcerated populations, an experience that strengthened my commitment to reducing barriers to treatment and supporting individuals who are often overlooked.

In addition to my behavioral health background, my experience as an Administrative Assistant at Lattes on Location strengthened my organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to coordinate multiple responsibilities while maintaining clear communication. My positions as a Registered Behavior Technician with Action Behavior Centers and Teacher Assistant with SESI Schools further developed my ability to work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams, adapt to individual needs, and remain calm and compassionate in challenging situations.

I recognize that reaching out for substance use treatment can be an incredibly vulnerable experience, not only for the individual seeking help but also for their loved ones. I believe the admissions process should be welcoming, informative, and free of judgment. My experience building rapport, communicating with individuals from diverse backgrounds, and coordinating care has prepared me to provide that level of support while ensuring timely follow-up and accurate documentation.

I am also pursuing my education in Addiction Studies, which reflects my long-term commitment to working with individuals affected by substance use disorders and co-occurring mental health conditions. Principles Recovery Center's emphasis on individualized treatment aligns closely with my professional values and the type of meaningful work I hope to continue throughout my career.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, strong communication skills, and passion for addiction recovery to Principles Recovery Center. I look forward to discussing how I can contribute to your admissions team and help individuals take those important first steps toward recovery.

Sincerely,

Taylor Cowles-Kokofsky

To whom this may concern:

Please accept this letter as my application for the available position with your organization. I am excited about the opportunity to contribute my extensive experience in community advocacy, behavioral health support, client engagement, and compassionate service delivery to an organization committed to improving the lives of individuals and communities.

I bring over ten years of customer service experience and nearly eight years of experience providing peer support, community advocacy, and supportive services to individuals and families experiencing homelessness, financial hardship, mental health challenges, and substance use concerns. Throughout my career, I have developed strong skills in client rapport building, active listening, motivational interviewing techniques, crisis prevention, information gathering, resource navigation, client intake assessments, and providing individualized support to individuals facing complex life circumstances.

My professional background has provided me with experience supporting individuals during emotionally challenging situations while maintaining empathy, professionalism, and a calm presence. I have conducted client interactions, completed needs assessments, provided community resource referrals, documented client services, utilized HMIS systems, and assisted individuals in accessing behavioral health, housing, and social service resources. I understand the importance of building a trusting working alliance with clients through respectful communication, validation, problem-solving, and client-centered support.

I am currently pursuing my Bachelor of Science in Psychology through Grand Canyon University’s online program. My academic studies are expanding my knowledge of human behavior, mental health concepts, crisis response strategies, and evidence-informed approaches to supporting individuals experiencing emotional distress. I am committed to continued professional development and building a long-term career within the behavioral health and human services field.

My qualifications include strong verbal and written communication skills, proficiency with Microsoft Office and Excel, medical terminology knowledge, virtual communication experience, appointment coordination, detailed record keeping, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in fast-paced environments. I am comfortable utilizing technology to communicate with clients and teams while maintaining confidentiality, accuracy, and professionalism.

I am passionate about helping individuals feel heard, supported, and connected to meaningful resources. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, education, and dedication to client-centered care can contribute positively to your organization.
Thank you for your time and consideration. Attached is my full resume. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss my qualifications further.

Sincerely,
Anya N. Townsend

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Principles Recovery Center. With over five years of experience in behavioral health administration, intake coordination, and client support, I bring a strong understanding of the admissions process, substance use treatment, and the importance of helping individuals and families navigate the path toward recovery.

In my work as an Intake Coordinator and Consultant with Transformative Health & Wellness, I have managed incoming inquiries, coordinated referrals, supported clients through the intake process, maintained accurate records, and collaborated with clinical teams to facilitate access to care. My experience working with behavioral health services, including IOP programs and substance use disorder treatment, has strengthened my ability to communicate compassionately, assess client needs, and help individuals navigate treatment options and next steps.

I understand that the admissions process is often a critical first point of connection for individuals seeking treatment. I approach these conversations with empathy, professionalism, and a strong commitment to follow-through, recognizing that timely communication and consistent support can make a meaningful difference in whether someone accesses the care they need.

In addition to my direct intake and coordination experience, I am highly organized, comfortable managing multiple priorities independently, and experienced in tracking referrals, maintaining documentation, coordinating appointments, and supporting efficient administrative workflows. While I may not have worked with every specific platform listed in the posting, I have experience with comparable systems and am confident in my ability to learn new EMR and CRM software quickly while maintaining accuracy, confidentiality, and HIPAA compliance.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my behavioral health experience, strong communication skills, and dedication to client-centered care to Principles Recovery Center. I am especially interested in contributing to a team that helps individuals access meaningful treatment and supports them as they take important steps toward recovery.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Pilar

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager, 
	My name is Elizabeth (Lizzy) Shafer. I am a Colorado native from Pueblo and have lived in Colorado Springs for 7 years where I went to school to obtain a dual Bachelors degree in Psychology and Philosophy. I worked full time as well as went to school full time. I work amazing under pressure, in fact I thrive under it. I am looking to continue my education in psychology, preparing for an online masters program in the upcoming spring semester. I am looking to continue to grow my resume in the mental health field and find a job that fits well. I worked for a year as a Social Emotional Wellness Specialist at Harrison Highschool in Colorado Springs where I did casework, worked closely with the kids to monitor progression of behavioral and mental health issues, and helped with school work. I took on a caseworker role for a few months even without the licensure. I was the crisis navigator being the first call during a mental health crisis, and I was also a one on one para to kids and a tutor for many others. During this time I created very close relationships with many of the kids and I loved being able to help them and make a difference in their lives. Unfortunately, I did not wish to continue to work in a position with no clear instructions. It was the first year that this position was granted and it was apparent in how many shoes I was expected to fill with no clear direction. The staff was constantly praiseful, even now I will still receive messages from the staff asking for advice on how to deal with many of the kids that I formed a close relationship with. I loved the impact I made, but was looking for something more structured. 
	I see myself working with individuals who are suffering from a crisis. I deal very well with people who may not click with everyone else. I love to be able to find that human connection with people who have maybe struggled in the past. I have experience in casework, case management, crisis management, teamwork, substance abuse disorder, court systems, long term care plans, and connecting with individuals who may not have many people to help them. I am a team player and I am always able to take charge when needed, I find myself filling leadership positions constantly even when I do not desire to. I know whatever team I am a part of will always strive for success and work well together. I am excited to hear back and hopefully be a part of the team!
Warmest Regards,
Elizabeth Shafer

Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator - Mental Health position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. 

My background combines behavioral health intake and case management with patient access, authorization, financial, and front desk operations.

Sincerely,

My experience at Metrolina Pain and Dependency provided direct exposure to substance use disorder treatment, particularly medication-assisted treatment for opioid dependence. Working in this setting strengthened my understanding of addiction recovery, patient confidentiality, treatment engagement, and the importance of accessible, coordinated services for individuals with complex behavioral health needs.

At Alexander Youth Network, I developed a strong foundation in behavioral health case management and treatment coordination while supporting adolescents with significant psychiatric, emotional, and behavioral needs. I collaborated with multidisciplinary teams, monitored client progress, maintained clinical documentation, communicated emerging concerns, and supported individualized treatment planning. This role required strong attention to detail, effective communication, sound judgment, and the ability to manage competing client needs in a fast-paced clinical environment.

My experience as a Sexual Trauma Advocate with Safe Passage further strengthened my capabilities in trauma-informed case management, client advocacy, needs identification, crisis response, and community resource coordination. I supported individuals navigating sensitive and often urgent circumstances, helping them understand available resources and access appropriate services. These responsibilities required discretion, compassionate communication, strong organizational skills, and consistent attention to client safety and continuity of care.

Across these positions, I have developed the core competencies essential to successful behavioral health admissions: building rapport, identifying client needs, gathering sensitive information, maintaining confidential records, coordinating services, communicating with treatment teams, and helping individuals navigate complex systems of care. My suicide crisis intervention certification further supports my ability to recognize safety concerns and respond appropriately to individuals experiencing emotional or psychiatric distress.

I am particularly interested in Principles Recovery Center because this position aligns closely with my experience in addiction treatment and behavioral health case management. I understand the importance of responsive communication, timely follow-through, accurate documentation, and creating a supportive admissions experience for individuals seeking treatment. I am prepared to apply these skills to coordinating intake assessments, managing prospective client communications, supporting referral relationships, and facilitating access to PHP and IOP services. I would bring a compassionate, detail-oriented, and highly organized approach to supporting admissions operations and helping individuals take the first step toward recovery.

candidates.cover_letter:
I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Principles Recovery Center. With professional experience in mental health care, a Medical Assistant certification, and a deeply personal understanding of the impact substance use can have on individuals and families, I am passionate about helping people access the care and support they need to begin their recovery journey.

My experience in mental health care has strengthened my ability to communicate compassionately, navigate sensitive situations, and recognize the importance of providing a supportive, nonjudgmental environment. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be an incredibly vulnerable experience, and I believe every individual deserves to be met with patience, dignity, and genuine understanding. I would bring these values to every interaction with prospective clients and their loved ones.

Beyond my professional background, my connection to substance use treatment is deeply personal. Growing up with a close family member affected by substance use shaped my understanding of addiction and its impact on family dynamics, emotional well-being, and personal relationships. It also influenced my own relationship with alcohol, encouraging me to approach it with greater awareness, intentionality, and responsibility. These experiences have given me a unique perspective on the importance of recovery, the courage it takes to seek help, and the difference compassionate support can make.

What particularly draws me to Principles Recovery Center is the opportunity to serve as an initial point of contact for individuals seeking treatment. I recognize that the admissions process is more than scheduling appointments or completing paperwork. It is often someone’s first step toward changing their life. I would take that responsibility seriously, ensuring that prospective clients and families feel informed, supported, and respected throughout the process.

I am confident that my communication skills, attention to detail, ability to work independently, and commitment to mental health advocacy would allow me to contribute positively to your admissions team. Most importantly, I would bring a sincere dedication to helping individuals take meaningful steps toward recovery.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to further discuss how my professional background and personal experiences align with the mission and values of Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,
Alexia Davis

Pastoral Letter of Recommendation
To Whom it may concern:
It is my privilege to offer my strongest personal and pastoral recommendation for Maria Turell.
As her pastor, I have had the opportunity to know Maria beyond what can be reflected on a
résumé or demonstrated during an interview. I have personally observed her character, her
values, the way she relates to others, and the integrity with which she carries herself when
entrusted with responsibility.
Maria is a woman of exceptional character. She is dependable, compassionate, respectful, and
genuinely concerned for the well-being of others. She has the ability to make people feel heard
and valued while maintaining professionalism, discretion, and good judgment. She takes her
responsibilities seriously, follows through on her commitments, and can be trusted to act with
integrity. These qualities are not simply professional attributes; they are part of who she is.
Over the years, Maria has served actively in several areas within our congregation. She has
provided direct support to our pastoral leadership, made follow-up and care calls to members and
families, visited those who are sick, accompanied and transported individuals to medical
appointments, and helped plan and coordinate church events and activities. These responsibilities
have consistently demonstrated her initiative, organization, sensitivity, reliability, and ability to
respond to the needs of others.
What particularly stands out about Maria is that she does not simply express concern for people;
she takes action. She follows up, makes herself available, and willingly gives of her own time to
support and assist others. In a healthcare environment, where people are often encountered
during vulnerable or stressful moments, I believe these qualities are especially valuable. Skills
can be developed and procedures can be taught, but character, compassion, and trustworthiness
are much harder to teach. Maria brings those qualities with her.
I would have complete confidence placing Maria in a position requiring responsibility,
discretion, teamwork, organization, and direct interaction with people. I am confident that she
would not merely fulfill the responsibilities entrusted to her, but would also contribute positively
to the organization she represents.
For these reasons, I recommend Maria without reservation and with my full confidence. Any
organization fortunate enough to have her as part of its team will be gaining not only a capable
professional, but a person of integrity, initiative, and genuine character.
Should you wish to speak with me personally regarding this recommendation, I would be pleased
to so.
Sincerely,
